attrs.reasoning: PT tutorials gloss the form `action` directly as 'ação'. Identical in pt-BR and pt-PT under AO90 (pre-AO90 'acção' obsolete since 2009/2015).
Standard gloss for the HTTP verb in every PT form tutorial checked. No regional variation.

Established PT noun for a programming trigger — title of the pt.wikipedia article on DB triggers, used unglossed in DevMedia/Trybe material. PT htmx articles use the verb 'acionadas', making 'acionador'/'disparador' plausible alternates, neither more recognisable.
MDN pt-BR translates event target as 'alvo'. A PT htmx guide uses 'elemento de destino', so 'destino' is a real synonym worth adding as an alternate.
PT htmx write-ups use exactly this verb for this concept ('o HTMX trocará o conteúdo pela nova resposta'). Observed usage, not a dictionary guess. 'substituição' is a sensible registered alternate.

events.reasoning: 'evento de clique' is near-universal in PT tutorials. Noun. Ordering correct: 'clique' before the infinitive 'clicar'. Same token in both variants.
Both attested nouns. Beginner-facing pt-BR material leads with 'mudança'; the pt-PT reference says 'Um elemento de HTML mudou'. Ordering suggestion only, nothing to remove.

'envio do formulário' dominant in pt-BR; noun, so primary is correct. The alternate 'submeter' is an infinitive — pt-PT says 'o utilizador submete', so registering the noun 'submissão' would serve European readers better.

No direct evidence of any PT name for the input event specifically — every source writes 'o evento input' in English. 'entrada' is the settled PT word for input generally and is a noun. Low-confidence-but-harmless rather than corroborated.

IMPERATIVE. 'focar' is a bare infinitive naming an action to perform, and is the odd one out next to noun siblings like 'clique'. Sources describe the event with the noun ('o elemento recebe o foco'). Single token, so it works in both positions.

IMPERATIVE. PT describes this as 'perda de foco' / 'quando um elemento perde o foco'. No clean single-token noun exists: 'desfoque' keeps al-desfoque writable but in web dev overwhelmingly means the CSS visual blur effect (same collision as ja/ko); 'perda de foco' is exactly what sources say but is multi-word. Recommend 'desfoque' primary with 'perda de foco' as an accepted alternate. NOTE: multi-word is now known to work in attribute names hyphenated, so 'perda de foco' is more viable than this finding assumed.

IMPERATIVE — 'iniciar' reads as 'start this', the opposite of 'this element was initialized'. No tutorial evidence exists because init is not a DOM event, so this is a register/consistency correction. 'início' is a shorter alternate.

Prior structural conclusion now SOURCED: MDN pt-BR 'um botão... é pressionado sobre um elemento'; pt-PT 'o botão esquerdo do rato é pressionado para baixo'. Contrary datum recorded: one informal pt-BR tutorial glosses onmousedown as 'quando o mouse for pra baixo', but that explains the English name rather than naming the event.
Confirmed for pt-BR. pt-PT uses a different verb — 'o botão esquerdo do rato é libertado' — so 'rato libertado' should be added as an alias.

IMPERATIVE. Observed noun is 'rolagem' ('o evento de rolagem do scroll', 'barra de rolagem'). Single token. Regional note: European standard is 'deslocamento', though 'rolagem' appears on Portugal-facing pages.
IMPERATIVE. The noun is what PT articles use for the event ('Detectando o redimensionamento da janela com JavaScript'). Single token, no regional variation.

candidates.reasoning: Heavily attested fixed collocation. 'tecla baixo' is an ungrammatical calque; 'pressionar tecla' is an infinitive command. Structurally consistent with 'mouse pressionado'.

Sources describe keyup as the key being released — 'a tecla é liberada' (BR), 'o utilizador liberta uma tecla' (PT). Register 'tecla liberada' as an alternate; it is the more common pt-BR wording and folding will not cover it.
Real usage backs the preposition: 'ao passar o mouse sobre um botão' (BR), 'move o rato sobre um elemento' (PT). Registering 'passar o mouse' as an alternate would match how beginners say it.
No direct collocation found; PT says 'sai com o mouse de um elemento'. Still transparent and pairs with 'mouse sobre'. Consider 'saída do mouse' or 'mouse saiu' as a better-evidenced alternate.

CROSS-VARIANT TRAP. Beyond the infinitive problem, in European Portuguese 'carregar' means to press ('carregar no botão'; the pt-PT tutorial glosses onkeydown as 'o utilizador carrega numa tecla'), so fx-gatilho="carregar" would read as a click/keypress to a Portuguese reader.

variantSplit.reasoning: All five attribute names are written identically in Brazil and Portugal — the reassuring half, and the half that matters most since attributes appear on every element. Divergence is confined to one lexical family: the pointing device, 'mouse' in Brazil and 'rato' in Portugal, affecting the four mouse* events; 'libertado' vs 'solto'/'liberado' rides along on mouseup. Scroll is softer — 'deslocamento' is the European standard for the scrollbar but 'rolagem' also appears on Portugal-facing pages, a preference rather than an intelligibility barrier. None of this justifies a pt-BR/pt-PT split: loka's parse maps are many-to-one, so registering 'rato pressionado', 'rato libertado', 'rato sobre', 'rato fora' and 'deslocamento' as additional keys in the same pt map makes European spellings work at zero runtime cost, with primary-first ordering keeping the Brazilian forms as the taught ones.

overall: The dominant finding is a FORM problem, not a word-choice problem: five of eleven shipped event terms (focar, desfocar, iniciar, rolar, redimensionar) are bare infinitives naming an action to perform, while the other six are nouns — and Portuguese has well-attested deverbal nouns for every one (foco, rolagem, redimensionamento; inicialização by analogy). Fixing those five would make the vocabulary internally consistent and stop terms reading as commands. The concluded 'mouse pressionado'/'mouse solto' now have real sources and should stand; the same participle pattern extends to keydown/keyup as 'tecla pressionada'/'tecla solta'. Two things the brief did not ask: 'carregar' for load is a genuine cross-variant trap, and 'desfoque' for blur collides with the CSS visual blur effect.
